key_concepts: Electron transfer leaves one object negatively charged and the other positively charged
Like charges repel and opposite charges attract
A charged balloon can stick to a neutral wall by induced charge separation
Negative charges in a wall move away from a negatively charged balloon
Different materials build up different amounts of static charge
Water mist or damp weather can discharge static electricity
Charged objects can attract light neutral objects such as confetti and paper
A charged balloon can bend a thin stream of water
A charged balloon can move an empty can without touching it
The triboelectric series helps predict electron movement between materials
Static electricity experiments work best in dry weather
